title: Passenger Chemical Oxygen Generator — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the passenger chemical oxygen generator removal task.

abstract: Removal of a chemical oxygen generator from a passenger service unit, with the firing pin safety, the handling restrictions and the disposal route for a generator that cannot be reinstalled.

sections.purpose: To remove a chemical oxygen generator from a passenger service unit for replacement, for expiry or for access to the unit behind it.
sections.job_setup_note: The cabin must be out of service and the passenger service unit panel dropped. The generator firing pin must be safetied before anything is disconnected. Oxygen-clean hands and tools are required: no grease, no oil and no hand cream. One person can do the task but a second must witness the safety pin installation.
sections.procedure: WARNING: A CHEMICAL OXYGEN GENERATOR CAN FIRE IF THE LANYARD IS PULLED. INSTALL THE SAFETY PIN BEFORE ANY OTHER WORK AND HAVE THE INSTALLATION WITNESSED. Make sure that the cabin is out of service and that the area below the unit is clear. Drop the passenger service unit panel and support it on the lanyard. Install the firing pin safety and have it witnessed. WARNING: DO NOT USE GREASE, OIL OR HAND CREAM NEAR AN OXYGEN COMPONENT. CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE IGNITION. Disconnect the mask hoses from the generator manifold one at a time and cap each port as it is freed. Disconnect the firing lanyard at the actuator D3520120132145 and secure it clear. Release the two generator retaining straps. Support the generator and remove it from the cradle. Examine the generator for discolouration at the end cap and record any finding. Put the generator in the transit container in the horizontal attitude and label it with the aircraft, the position and the date. CAUTION: DO NOT STACK GENERATORS IN THE TRANSIT CONTAINER. THE CONTAINER IS DESIGNED FOR A SINGLE LAYER.
sections.close_out: Make sure that every mask hose port is capped and that no hose is left hanging. Make sure that the firing lanyard is secured clear of the cradle. Fit the blanking cradle cover if a generator is not being installed immediately. Raise and latch the passenger service unit panel. Record the removal, the generator part number, the expiry date and any finding. Route an expired or discoloured generator to the operator hazardous material procedure; it must not be returned to stores.

safety_precautions: A chemical oxygen generator can fire if the lanyard is pulled. Install the safety pin first and have it witnessed.
Do not use grease, oil or hand cream near an oxygen component.
Support the passenger service unit panel on the lanyard.

title: Passenger Chemical Oxygen Generator — Removal

issue.reason: Warning added against leaving two generator standards in one service unit, which until now was stated only in the modification and the bulletin.

abstract: Removal of a chemical oxygen generator from a passenger service unit, with the firing pin safety, the prohibition on a mixed standard within one unit, the handling restrictions and the disposal route.

sections.purpose: To remove a chemical oxygen generator from a passenger service unit for replacement, for expiry or for access to the unit behind it.
sections.job_setup_note: The cabin must be out of service and the passenger service unit panel dropped. The generator firing pin must be safetied before anything is disconnected. Oxygen-clean hands and tools are required: no grease, no oil and no hand cream. One person can do the task but a second must witness the safety pin installation. Before a generator is taken out, note the duration standard of every generator in the same service unit and plan what will replace it: a service unit may not be left with a twelve minute and a twenty-two minute generator side by side, and the technician at the aircraft is the only person in a position to see that it has happened.
sections.procedure: WARNING: A CHEMICAL OXYGEN GENERATOR CAN FIRE IF THE LANYARD IS PULLED. INSTALL THE SAFETY PIN BEFORE ANY OTHER WORK AND HAVE THE INSTALLATION WITNESSED. Make sure that the cabin is out of service and that the area below the unit is clear. Drop the passenger service unit panel and support it on the lanyard. WARNING: A PASSENGER SERVICE UNIT MUST NOT BE LEFT WITH GENERATORS OF TWO DIFFERENT DURATION STANDARDS. RECORD THE STANDARD OF EVERY GENERATOR IN THE UNIT BEFORE ONE IS REMOVED, AND DO NOT CLOSE THE UNIT UNTIL EVERY POSITION IN IT CARRIES THE SAME STANDARD. Install the firing pin safety and have it witnessed. WARNING: DO NOT USE GREASE, OIL OR HAND CREAM NEAR AN OXYGEN COMPONENT. CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE IGNITION. Disconnect the mask hoses from the generator manifold one at a time and cap each port as it is freed. Disconnect the firing lanyard at the actuator D3520120132145 and secure it clear. Release the two generator retaining straps. Support the generator and remove it from the cradle. Examine the generator for discolouration at the end cap and record any finding. Put the generator in the transit container in the horizontal attitude and label it with the aircraft, the position and the date. CAUTION: DO NOT STACK GENERATORS IN THE TRANSIT CONTAINER. THE CONTAINER IS DESIGNED FOR A SINGLE LAYER.
sections.close_out: Make sure that every mask hose port is capped and that no hose is left hanging. Make sure that the firing lanyard is secured clear of the cradle. Confirm and record that every generator position in the service unit carries the same duration standard. Fit the blanking cradle cover if a generator is not being installed immediately. Raise and latch the passenger service unit panel. Record the removal, the generator part number, the expiry date and any finding. Route an expired or discoloured generator to the operator hazardous material procedure; it must not be returned to stores.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The strap arrangement differs on aircraft post MOD-111284.

safety_precautions: A chemical oxygen generator can fire if the lanyard is pulled. Install the safety pin first and have it witnessed.
Do not use grease, oil or hand cream near an oxygen component.
Support the passenger service unit panel on the lanyard.
